newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks dip slightly despite plunge in Dow.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks dip slightly despite plunge in Dow.

text.p: Brazilian stocks dipped slightly lower on Thursday in moderate trade, mostly shrugging off a plunge on Wall Street, traders said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most-active stocks fell 0.03 percent to 9314 on volume of 591 million reais ($562 million).
"I was surprised we didn't come off more, especially with the Dow down 140 points in late session. But we had enough buyers to sustain the market," said one trader.
Bluechips were up or down slightly across the board. As has been the case most of the week, there was no particular news affecting individual stocks, traders said.
Benchmark Telebras preferred shares closed up 0.09 percent at 112, with common shares losing 1.02 percent to 106.

Brazil's high court once again delayed a ruling on the constitutionality of selling off concessions of B Band cellular service to the private sector. The court was expected to decide the issue on March 19.
CVRD preferred shares fell 0.77 percent to close at 25.90 and common shares were off 0.64 percent at 31.10.
Petrobras preferred shares gained 0.47 percent at 213, with common shares down 1.68 percent at 174.

The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index (IEE) dipped 0.35 percent to close at 2599. The index, which includes the nine most liquid power stocks, was held steady by state-owned power company Eletrobras, whose preferred shares were unchanged at 490.
